first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ, both directly matching the mechanisms in memory_31 (signup simplification lifting first-week activation) and memory_86 (shortened onboarding improving completion and time-to-value). These are durable, previously-validated self-serve levers that directly counter the current metric declines without engaging in a margin-eroding price war. Promotional pricing (memory_73) could counter the competitor's move short-term, but matching aggressive entry pricing risks attracting less qualified, price-sensitive accounts that conflict with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, and that tradeoff isn't well-characterized in the existing memory. I'm verifying memory_31 and memory_86 because they're the two most load-bearing records for the action I intend to take, and I want to confirm the original experiments actually measured durable activation/completion lift rather than short-term signal before committing this week's single experiment slot to a broad or aggressive rollout.

final.rationale: Verified sources confirm both memories: exp_31 (signup simplification) delivered activation +9% and qualified revenue +4% on SMB, though with a small -1% retention dip and explicit note it 'holds on SMB; not replicated on other segments.' exp_86 (shortened onboarding) confirmed completion +13%, time-to-value improvement, and retention +3%. Together these directly target this quarter's two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) with a self-serve lever that doesn't require racing the competitor's pricing cuts, which risks attracting low-quality, price-sensitive accounts contrary to sustainable qualified revenue. I'm flagging downstream_value_risk because exp_31 traded a small retention decrease for revenue/activation gains — worth watching if combined with onboarding shortening, since compounding time-to-value cuts could stack retention risk even though the individual effects are net positive and confirmed. I'm running this as a standard_experiment (not broad rollout) specifically scoped to SMB self-serve, since that's the only segment where the mechanism is verified; broader segments remain unproven per the source record. This preserves the option to reassess promotional pricing or enterprise-assist as a second-priority experiment next cycle if competitive SMB attrition continues.
